detailed_description:
The final video must be one single continuous cinematic frame filling the entire screen; no grid, split screen, panels, collage, dividing lines, panel numbers, or any multi-image composition.
The source video must contain no generated subtitles, captions, titles, labels, logos, watermarks, UI text, or any other readable text; all approved text must be added only in post-production.
The panels in the reference storyboard indicate only the chronological order of actions and narrative keyframes; never render panel borders, dividing lines, numbers, or side-by-side multiple panels in the final video.
Live-action mythic Chinese epic cinema inside Zixiao Palace: cool celadon stone, charcoal shadows, restrained antique-gold light from the high dais, believable skin and silk, soft highlight roll-off, subtle film grain. Keep the audience-side camera on the hall center axis with one very slow motivated push that settles by 7.8 seconds; no orbit, drift or reframing after it settles.
From 0.00 to 1.80 seconds, the composition makes the count unambiguous: exactly six separate cushions in one front row. From screen left to right, Laozi occupies cushion one, Yuanshi occupies cushion two, Tongtian occupies cushion three, Nuwa occupies cushion four, cushion five is empty, and cushion six is empty. No additional cushion, duplicate body or replacement sitter appears. Dijun stands beside the left midground column and occupies no cushion. Hongyun stands in the rear center and Zhenyuanzi in the rear right, both visibly separated from the two empty cushions.
From 1.80 to 3.20 seconds, after the empty pair becomes readable, Dijun's eyes move first from cushions five and six toward Hongyun and Zhenyuanzi; his head follows by only a small amount while his shoulders and weight remain relaxed. His lips remain naturally closed because the line is internal narration. A faint tightening of the lower eyelid begins, peaks briefly, then releases into the social mask.
From 3.20 to 6.80 seconds, <Subject 5> says in an off-screen internal voiceover, <d>[zh-CN] 看来上次他俩哭爹喊娘的也没能让鸿钧收为座下弟子，这次听道，连蒲团都不敢坐了。</d> Hongyun notices the glance after a short delay, lowers his eyes toward the floor beside the empty cushions, makes one small backward weight adjustment, then becomes still. Zhenyuanzi reacts later and independently: his eyes check Hongyun without turning his torso, then return toward the dais. They never turn, blink, nod or shift weight on the same beat. The four seated figures remain four distinct people in their assigned seats; their subdued breathing, gaze refocus and irregular blinks occur at different times and never become a synchronized group gesture.
From 6.80 to 8.20 seconds, on the final clause, only one corner of Dijun's mouth lifts slightly while the jaw stays relaxed; the change reaches a brief low-amplitude peak and releases, leaving a controlled trace of private irony. Hair, sleeve hems and crown tassels move only from breathing or the existing faint hall air, with smaller delayed motion that damps naturally; no windless flutter.
From 8.20 to 9.00 seconds, hold the verified result: seats one through four remain occupied by the same four people, seats five and six remain empty, Dijun remains left midground, Hongyun rear center and Zhenyuanzi rear right. No one approaches or sits on an empty cushion. No purple energy, portal, arrow, annotation, random text or invented figure appears.
The final video must be one single continuous cinematic frame filling the entire screen; no grid, split screen, panels, collage, dividing lines, panel numbers, or any multi-image composition.

Duck the hall tone gently under the voice without removing it. Hongyun's weight shift creates one soft rear-center fabric-and-sole sound synchronized to the visible movement. No visible mouth speaks, no energy hum, no crane-wing effect and no undeclared music.
